what_its_for: Methenamine hippurate is used to prevent urinary tract infections (UTIs) from coming back. It works by releasing a substance in your urine that kills bacteria in your bladder. It is NOT used to treat an active infection — only to prevent new ones from starting.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with food or milk to help prevent an upset stomach. Swallow the tablet whole or you may crush it and mix it with food or liquid if you have trouble swallowing. Take it at the same times each day to keep it working consistently. Make sure to drink plenty of fluids (at least 6 to 8 glasses of water daily) unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 gram (one tablet) taken twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening. For children 6 to 12 years old, the usual dose is 500 mg to 1 gram twice a day. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in a dry place away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) or potassium citrate while on this medicine, as they can make your urine less acidic and stop the medicine from working properly. Limit foods and drinks that make your urine less acidic, such as large amounts of citrus fruits, juices, or milk. Avoid sulfonamide antibiotics (like sulfamethoxazole) at the same time unless specifically directed by your doctor, as this combination can cause crystals to form in your urine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat; painful or burning urination, frequent urination, or blood in your urine (possible signs of a new UTI); severe stomach pain or nausea; skin rash or unusual bruising; or any new or worsening symptoms. Also call your doctor if you feel the medicine is not working or if infections keep coming back.
when_it_works: This medicine works best over time as a preventive measure. It starts releasing its active ingredient in your urine within a few hours of taking it, but it is meant to be taken every day on a long-term basis to keep bacteria from growing in your bladder. You may not feel any different while taking it — that is normal. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Do not use this medicine if you have severe kidney disease or liver problems, as it may build up in your body and cause harm. Older adults: Use with caution; your doctor may monitor you more closely. Children under 6 years old: This medicine is generally not recommended for very young children. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medicines before starting this medication.
